hints: Look carefully at the two pictures. The left one is a transverse section through the central stele of a root, the right one is a longitudinal section of the other organ. Where are the big empty xylem vessels and where are the clusters of tiny thin-walled cells?

Remember which cells always work side by side. Companion cells are only ever found with sieve tube elements in phloem, so you are looking for a small phloem cell in the root section, not a large lignified xylem vessel.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two organs and tissues**

Hello, let us start by reading the pictures. The left photomicrograph is a TS of a root. You can see the small central vascular stele surrounded by a wide cortex. The right photomicrograph is a LS of a different organ, showing long vertical files of cells.

**Recall where companion cells live**

Companion cells are the metabolic helpers of sieve tube elements. They are always found together in phloem tissue. So the question is really asking, where is a sieve tube element in the phloem of the root?

**Spot xylem versus phloem in the root TS**

In the root TS, xylem vessels are very large, round, empty cells with thick dark walls in the centre. Phloem is the groups of much smaller, thin-walled, crowded cells between the arms of xylem. Label A points to a big xylem vessel. Label B points to the small cells of the phloem cluster. That is the sieve tube and companion cell tissue, so B is the answer.

options.A: A points to a large metaxylem vessel in the centre of the root stele, a water-conducting xylem cell with no companion cells.
options.B: B points to the small thin-walled cells of phloem in the root transverse section. This is where sieve tube elements are found together with companion cells.
options.C: C points to a long cell in the longitudinal section of the other organ, not to phloem in the root transverse section.
options.D: D points to a xylem vessel element in longitudinal section, recognised by its spiral lignified thickening for water transport, not phloem.
